keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1320-1322: Cliopatria's Tughlaq row starts in 1326 and its Khalji row runs to 1325, but the dynasty is 'Established: 8 September 1320' (infobox; Lahrawat 6 September, Delhi Sultanate page). The Khalji outline of 1317-1320 (no Bengal, Devagiri in) carries over: 7915 cells, about 2.04 M km2. fx-12 (2026-11-01), trimmed of land that pages show under local dynasties and no Delhi governor in these years (hierarchy fixes F070 F121 F135 F149 F303 F304 F305): Lower Sindh: the Soomra page lists the Soomra emirs Khafif III (1315-1333) to Hamir II (1341-1351) and says they were 'probably centered in lower Sindh'; the Samma page has 'in 1333 the Sammas were in rebellion' (Ibn Battuta), 'The Sammas overthrew the Soomras soon after 1335' and the capital at Thatta, and no page opened has Delhi governing lower Sindh before Muhammad bin Tughluq's 1351 expedition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samma_dynasty, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soomra_dynasty, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Sindh). Reviewer fx-12 (2026-11-01): the same Samma page also has Ibn Battuta observe in 1333 a 'Samma rebellion against the Delhi government' and the last Soomra ruler 'under the protection of Muhammad bin Tughluq', so Delhi claimed overlordship in lower Sindh; the trim draws the local dynasties' hold, not a Delhi loss, and the Delhi claim is a matter for hierarchy.csv. The extent (Thatta within 220 km, inside Sind) is my reading; upper Sind stays in the outline. Jaisalmer: after Alauddin Khalji's siege 'the fort remained under the sway of Delhi Sultanate' only 'for a few years' before 'some surviving Bhatis' reoccupied it; the rulers are Rawal Gharsi Singh (1306-1335) and Kehar Singh II (1335-1402), and the page names no Tughlaq control (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaisalmer_State). Chhattisgarh: the Kalachuri kingdom of Ratnapura 'was unaffected by the Muslim invasions of the 13th-16th centuries' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalachuris_of_Ratnapura). Baghelkhand: 'Until the 15th century, the Baghela's of Bandhogarh were engaged in extending their possessions' and 'escaped the attention of the Delhi Sultans' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rewa_State). Hadoti: Rao Deva took Bundi in 1241 and 'for the next two centuries, the Hadas of Bundi were the vassals of the Sisodias of Mewar'; the page names no Delhi tie (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bundi_State). Dhundhar: the Kachhwaha rulers are Johnsi Dev (1317-1366), Udaikaran (1366-1388) and Narsingh (1388-1428), and the page names no Delhi tie (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_State). Marwar: the Rathores held Pali from 1243; 'Dhuhar captured Mandore from the Pariharas but lost it later' and Chunda received Mandore from a Parihar clan and moved there in 1395; the page names no Delhi governor (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Marwar).

ledger.note: 1347: the Deccan secedes. 'Bahmani revolt: 1347, led by Ala al-Din Hasan Bahman Shah' (a footnote); 'By 1347, the Deccan had revolted under Ismail Mukh' (Tughlaq page); 'By 1347, the Bahmani Sultanate had become independent' (Delhi Sultanate page). Firuz later 'recognised the Deccan's independence'.

region.text: Sind, the realm of the Sammas

ledger.note: 1351: Sind secedes. 'Muhammad bin Tughluq led an expedition against Sindh in 1351 and died at Sondha, possibly while trying to restore the Soomras. The Sammas then became independent' (Samma page); he died on 20 March 1351 on his way to Thatta (his page). Cliopatria gives Sind to the Sammas from 1344. This dossier keeps Sind (Cliopatria's 1344 Samma outline, 490 cells) to March 1351 because the Samma page has the Sammas in rebellion against the Delhi government in 1333 (Ibn Battuta), places their independence after 1351 and starts the dynasty in 1351. Open mirrors, for the orchestrator: soomra-dynasty draws the province of Sind (562 cells, 483 of them inside this dossier's 1344-1350 shape) as Soomra land to 1351, and sind-samma-dynasty /ledger/0 names soomra-dynasty, not this dossier, as its 1351 counterpart (its predecessors list both). I did not add a vassal_start for lower Sind: no page opened says the Soomras or Sammas were Delhi's vassals before 1351 (the Soomra page has Iltutmish only; the Samma infobox's tribute runs 1351-1388, see 1363). fx-12 (2026-11-01): lower Sindh round Thatta is no longer drawn as Delhi's before this loss (keyframes 1320-1350), because the Soomra and Samma pages show local dynasties there (see the 1320 keyframe's note); the loss now takes only the rest of the Samma outline.

region.text: Rajasthan with Ajmer, eastern Madhya Pradesh (Bundelkhand), Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar: the lands Cliopatria's Tughlaq shape drops in 1352 and that are in no later row (Malwa is kept in the outline to 1401)

ledger.note: 1352: Cliopatria's shape drops the plains south and east of the Delhi core (2,447 cells, about 0.62 M km2, once Malwa is kept in). Page silent: the Firuz Shah, Delhi Sultanate and Nasir-ud-Din pages record the Deccan (recognised independent), Bengal (not annexed) and Sind as outside and date no loss of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh or Bihar; the Tughlaq page has only 'The Rajput states also expelled the governor of Ajmer' (undated) and, after Firuz's death, 'anarchy and disintegration'. Malwa (585 cells) is cut out of this loss: it was governed for Delhi by Dilawar Khan to 1401 (Malwa Sultanate page; see 1401). The rest is a bridging judgment from Cliopatria's shape, kept at confidence 1. fx-12 (2026-11-01): Chhattisgarh, Baghelkhand, Jaisalmer, Pali-Mandore, Bundi-Kota and Dhundhar are no longer drawn as Delhi's from 1320 (keyframe 1320 note: the pages name local dynasties there and no Delhi governor), so this loss no longer takes them; it still takes the rest of the plains it lists, at confidence 1.

region.text: the region of the Rai of Jajpur, modern Odisha

ledger.note: 1360: Jajnagar pays tribute. Firuz 'invaded the region of the Rai of Jajpur (modern Odisha) in 1360. The Rai surrendered and promised an annual tribute of 20 elephants.' The Rai of Jajpur is the Eastern Ganga king in my reading; the Eastern Ganga dossier of sa-03 dates Firuz's Odisha invasion 1353-1358.

region.text: Thatta and the Samma rulers

ledger.note: 1363: Thatta submits. He 'set out for Thatta in 1362, but disease and food shortages forced a retreat to Gujarat. In 1363 he returned, and the rulers of Thatta submitted with an annual tribute of 400,000 tankas.' The Samma page has Firuz attack 'in 1365 and 1367 without success' and then obtain Banbhiniyo's surrender.

region.text: the region of the Rai of Jajpur

ledger.note: 1388: Firuz dies (20 September 1388) and the Jajnagar tribute is closed with his reign; the page records one levy and no continuing obligation. The Eastern Ganga page (opened 2026-10-20) has Firuz invading Odisha 'between 1353 and 1358' and levying tribute, and says nothing of a later tribute; the 1388 end stays a bridge (confidence 1).

region.text: Thatta and the Samma rulers

ledger.note: 1388: Firuz dies and the Thatta tribute is closed with his reign; the Samma page has the Sammas 'subject to Delhi for a time' without an end, and Cliopatria draws Sind as the Sammas' alone. The Samma page infobox lists 'Tributary relations with the Delhi Sultanate (1351-1388)'; the 1363 start is the Firuz page's, and the Samma text has Firuz's attacks of 1365 and 1367 'unsuccessful' before Banbhiniyo's surrender.

region.text: Jaunpur and Awadh under Malik Sarwar

ledger.note: 1394: Jaunpur is founded under Malik Sarwar. 'In 1394, he was appointed as the governor of Jaunpur' and the sultanate was 'founded in 1394 by Khwajah-i-Jahan Malik Sarwar' (Jaunpur page, infobox 'Established: 1394'); 'Soon, he established himself as an independent ruler' (undated), and his line first coined in its own name in 1402. The year is the page's founding year, not a dated secession (confidence 2); the Nasir-ud-Din page lists 'the Jaunpur Sultanate under Malik Sarwar in Awadh' among the breakaways, undated.

region.text: Gujarat under Muzaffar Shah I

ledger.note: 1394: Gujarat declares independence. 'The kingdom was established in 1394 when Muzaffar Shah I, the governor of Gujarat, declared independence' (Gujarat Sultanate page, infobox 'Declared independence from Delhi Sultanate: 1394'); the page has him appointed governor in 1391 and taking the royal title only in 1407. The Nasir-ud-Din page lists 'the Gujarat Sultanate under Muzaffar Shah I' among the breakaways, undated.

region.text: Delhi and Firozabad

ledger.note: 1394: two sultans. Sikandar Shah died on 8 March 1394; 'his relative Nusrat Shah challenged the succession, and the war lasted from 1394 to 1397. Mahmud ruled from Delhi while Nusrat Shah ruled from Firozabad.'

region.text: Delhi and Firozabad

ledger.note: 1397: the split ends. 'Mahmud Tughluq and Nusrat Shah both called themselves Sultan from 1394 to 1397'; the page does not say how Nusrat Shah's rule ended.

region.text: Delhi and the Doab round it

ledger.note: December 1398: Timur sacks Delhi. 'The Sack of Delhi took place on 17 December 1398' (infobox 17-20 December); Timur had 'crossed the Indus River' on 30 September and captured Multan in October. A raid, not an annexation.

region.text: Delhi

ledger.note: 1399: Timur leaves. 'Over fifteen days, Timur and his army raged a massacre ... Timur then returned to Samarkand with his loot.' The page gives no date of departure; fifteen days from 17 December 1398 puts it in the first days of 1399.

region.text: Malwa around Dhar under Dilawar Khan

ledger.note: 1401: Malwa becomes an independent realm. Dilawar Khan, 'the governor of Malwa for the Delhi Sultanate', 'had ceased to pay tribute to Delhi after 1392' and 'in 1401, made Malwa an independent realm' (Malwa Sultanate page; infobox 'Established: 1401', 'Preceded by: Delhi Sultanate'). The page dates his independence both ways ('asserted his independence in 1392', royal ensigns 'till 1401'); 1401 is kept to match the malwa-sultanate found. Malwa was crushed in 1338 when 'his nephew rebelled in Malwa' (Delhi Sultanate page) and stayed in the sultanate. The 26 cells of the Malwa region that lie in Mewar were never in the outline after 1336.

region.text: the Punjab, Multan and Dipalpur: the cells Cliopatria moves from the Tughlaq to the Timurid row

ledger.note: 1402: the Punjab passes to Timur's governor. Khizr Khan, 'governor of Multan', was 'appointed by Timur' and 'paid tribute to the Timurids at Samarkand'; he 'had initially controlled only Multan, Dipalpur, and parts of Sindh' (Tughlaq page). The year is Cliopatria's (its Timurid row takes the Punjab in 1402); the Battle of Delhi page has Multan captured in October 1398. The Khizr Khan page (opened 2026-10-20) has no 1402: its infobox gives him 'Governor of Multan' from 17 December 1398 to 28 May 1414 under Timur, and says he 'continued to pay him tribute' after Timur withdrew (undated). Multan was therefore Timurid-tributary from the sack of Delhi; the year for the whole Punjab stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: the north-west and west of the 1402 shape

ledger.counterpart: page silent: the Khokhars of the Punjab, the chiefs of Mewat and local governors
ledger.note: 1407: the north-west and west fall away. 'Punjab under the Khokhars (Shaikha Khokhar)' and 'Mewat under Khanzada Bahadur Khan' are named as breakaways, undated; Cliopatria shrinks the shape to Delhi and the Doab in 1407 (445 cells). The Daulat Khan Lodi page (opened 2026-10-20) is silent on 1405-1414, the Khokhars and Mewat; the year stays Cliopatria's (confidence 1).

region.text: Delhi and the Doab round it, passing to the Sayyid dynasty

ledger.note: 1414: Khizr Khan takes Delhi and the Tughlaq dynasty is over. He 'entered Delhi victoriously on 6 June 1414' and founded the Sayyid dynasty; the infobox says 'Disestablished: February 1413' (Mahmud, the last Tughlaq sultan, died in February 1413, Nasir-ud-Din page) and the lead 'ended in 1413'; the pages name no ruler of Delhi for the sixteen months between. The Khizr Khan page gives 28 May 1414 for his capture of Delhi and his anointment (infobox); the month 6 is the Tughlaq page's.

wars.name: Siege of Warangal (Tughlaq)
wars.outcome: A first raid in 1321 failed; the siege of 1323 took Warangal, renamed Sultanpur, and annexed the kingdom.
wars.note: The Tughlaq page dates the first raid to 1321 and the fall 'four months later'; the Muhammad bin Tughluq page has the siege in 1323.

wars.name: Ghiyath al-Din's Bengal campaign
wars.outcome: Bengal brought under Delhi, invited by the Muslim aristocracy of Lakhnauti.

wars.name: Hammir Singh's recovery of Mewar
wars.outcome: Hammir Singh 'attempted to regain control of Mewar, but his initial efforts were thwarted' from 1326 (Mewar page); he 'liberated the strategic Rajputana following the victory in Battle of Singoli in 1336' (Muhammad bin Tughluq page) and Mewar left the sultanate.
wars.note: The Mewar page dates the start (1326) and the Muhammad bin Tughluq page the end (1336); neither dates a campaign between.

wars.name: Conquest of Kampili
wars.outcome: Kampili destroyed; the enclave becomes Tughlaq land.

wars.name: Revolts against Muhammad bin Tughluq
wars.outcome: 'Revolts against Muhammad bin Tughlaq began in 1327'; Ma'bar 1334-35, Warangal 1336, Mewar 1336, Bengal by 1339, the Deccan 1347, Sind 1351. 'The geographical reach of the Sultanate shrunk particularly after 1335.'
wars.note: The Qarachil expedition of 1333 ended in defeat in the hills ('nearly all of the army perished') without moving the border; the Khurasan plan has no year.

wars.name: Firuz Shah's Bengal campaigns
wars.outcome: Invasion of Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah's Bengal in 1353: he withdrew to Ekdala and Firuz 'declined to annex'; a second march (the page dates it 1358, the Tughlaq page 'a war ... for 11 months in 1359') besieged Ekdala and ended in a peace with Sikandar Shah by which Zafar Khan regained Sonargaon. No border moved; Jaunpur was founded during the march (1358).

wars.name: Firuz Shah's Odisha and Thatta expeditions
wars.outcome: Jajpur surrendered in 1360 with a tribute of 20 elephants a year; Thatta submitted in 1363 (after a failed march in 1362) with 400,000 tankas a year. Tribute, not territory.

wars.name: Nusrat Shah's rebellion
wars.outcome: Two sultans for three years, Mahmud at Delhi and Nusrat Shah at Firozabad; how it ended is not on the pages.

wars.name: Timur's invasion of India
wars.outcome: Timur crossed the Indus on 30 September 1398, took Multan in October and sacked Delhi on 17-20 December ('the lowest point for the dynasty came in 1398'); he left without annexing Delhi and Multan passed to Khizr Khan under Timurid overlordship.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given by any page opened. The 1330-1335 peak, the Deccan and Bengal frontiers, and the Punjab and Rajasthan margins after 1352 are approximate; the Doab and Delhi core is the least uncertain.

notes: Tughlaq dynasty: nine Cliopatria shapes (1326-1414) reviewed against Tughlaq dynasty, Muhammad bin Tughluq, Firuz Shah Tughlaq, Battle of Delhi (1398), Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq and the Delhi Sultanate page (six pages, one over the budget of five; the Kampili and Samma pages opened for those states are also cited). Repaired 2026-10-20 after review: nine more pages were opened (Malwa, Mewar, Jaunpur, Gujarat, Madurai, Eastern Ganga, Khizr Khan, Daulat Khan Lodi, Soomra), so the budget is exceeded; the six main pages were re-read. (1) Dates: start 8 September 1320 (Cliopatria 1326: 1320-1325 are carried by three new keyframes built on the Khalji outline); end 6 June 1414 (the infobox says February 1413; Cliopatria 1414). (2) The big Cliopatria moves and what explains them: 1333-1344 (Tamil Nadu 1335, Warangal/Vijayanagara/Mewar 1336, Bengal 1339 explained by pages; Sind 1344 is the Samma row's start, the pages say 1351 and Sind is put back until then); 1344-1352 (the Deccan 1347 explained; Rajasthan with Ajmer, eastern Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, 2,447 cells (0.62 M km2), leave in 1352 with no page behind it: recorded as a confidence-1 loss to 'nobody'; Gujarat and Jaunpur are put back on page evidence, and Malwa (585 cells) stays Tughlaq until 1401 because the Malwa Sultanate page has Dilawar Khan governing it for the Delhi Sultanate until 1401; the corrected 1352 outline is 3,599 cells, 0.91 M km2, 0.33 of the infobox's 2.8 M km2 for 1350); 1395-1407 (Punjab 1402 explained in substance; the 1407 trim is page-silent). The Malwa, Gujarat, Jaunpur, Madurai, Eastern Ganga, Khizr Khan and Daulat Khan Lodi pages were opened in the repair: Jaunpur (1394, confidence 2) and Gujarat (1394, confidence 3) are now dated by their pages; the Ma'bar annexation year (1326), the end of the Odisha tribute (1388), the 1402 and 1407 Punjab and north-west losses and the 1352 drop of Rajasthan, Bundelkhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are still undated by any page. (3) Page disagreements: first Warangal raid and fall (1321 and 'four months later' on the Tughlaq page, 1323 on Muhammad's); Firuz's second Bengal campaign 1358 (his page) against 1359 (Tughlaq and Delhi Sultanate pages); Odisha 1360 (Firuz) against 1353-1358 (Eastern Ganga dossier); Thatta 1363 (Firuz) against 1365-1367 (Samma page); the Musunuri recovery of Warangal 1336 (Tughlaq page) against c. 1330 (Kakatiya dossier); the dynasty's end 1413 against 1414; the Delhi Sultanate page dates Khizr Khan's reign 1415-1451 while its lead says 1414. (4) Not modelled, no ground held or no date: Muhammad's Chittagong and Tipperah occupation ('occupied', no year), the Qarachil and Khurasan plans, Firuz's Kangra fief (the Rai of Kangra 'kept his territory as a fief', no year), the Gujarat iqta of 1377, Jaunpur's foundation in 1358, Mahmud's flight to Gujarat and Malwa and his return (not on the pages), Khandesh's separation; the nephew's revolt in Malwa in 1338 ('flayed alive') moved no border. (5) Counterparts that need or may need dossiers: balbani-sultanate-of-bengal (sa-04-a's slug; Shamsuddin Firoz Shah's Lakhnauti), nusrat-shah (the rival sultan at Firozabad 1394-1397: a city-sized rebel, low priority). The Eastern Ganga identification of the Rai of Jajpur is my reading. (6) Sind: the Soomra dossier ends in 1351 and the Samma dossier of this batch starts in 1351; this dossier keeps Sind with Delhi to 1351, against Cliopatria's 1344, on the Samma page (rebellion of 1333 against the Delhi government; independent after 1351). Three dossiers still claim the same cells: soomra-dynasty draws the province of Sind to 1351, sind-samma-dynasty names soomra-dynasty as its 1351 counterpart, and khalji-dynasty's 1314 shape carries Sind to 1320. I did not write a vassal for lower Sind: no page says the Soomras or Sammas were Delhi's vassals before 1351. (9) Mewar: 1326-1336 is a contest with kingdom-of-mewar (Mewar page 1326; Singoli 1336); kingdom-of-mewar must record the same contest or move its found to 1336. (10) Malwa: lost in 1401 to malwa-sultanate; the Malwa page also says Dilawar Khan 'asserted his independence in 1392' and paid no tribute after it, so a 1392-1393 date is arguable; 1401 is kept to match the Malwa dossier's found. (7) The Delhi Sultanate dynasties are one state in the Wikipedia sense; one hue for the family. (8) Region names the gazetteer lacks: Munger (used as a 60 km circle at 25.38 N 86.47 E). (11) fx-12 (2026-11-01): the Cliopatria outlines of 1320-1351 were trimmed of land the pages show under local dynasties (lower Sindh, Jaisalmer, Ratnapura, Baghelkhand, Bundi-Kota, Dhundhar, Pali-Mandore; Bundi and Dhundhar also in 1352-1407) and of the Guntur country south of the Krishna (1323-1346) and Warangal in 1344-1346; each is judged from pages that name local rulers and no Delhi governor, so it is a confidence-2 reading, not a dated loss. Open handoff for soomra-dynasty: it draws all of Sind to 1351 where its page says 'probably centered in lower Sindh'.
